title: Interpretations of Proverbs
english: Crows, mocking a father and dishonoring a mother in her old age, tore him away from the ravines, and young eagles devoured him.

These crows mystically feed the righteous, but they slaughter the unrighteous, gouging out the eyes of injustice, because they mocked the Father of all, who is God, and they dishonored the ancient knowledge that bore them. Regarding those gouging out the eyes, he called them crows; but regarding those devouring the whole man, he named them eagles, because one believes in a partial purification and the other in a total purification.
If the unpure are standing on the left of the Savior, and the goat leads these, let us hope the goat does not now signify the devil.
The weak will not be able to judge correctly if, by drinking, they forget wisdom.

Give a drink to those in sorrows and let those in pains drink wine, so that they may forget their poverty and may no longer remember their labors; for he who is intoxicated by the potency of the master's house forgets his pains.
Open your mouth and judge justly; but distinguish the poor and the weak. The poor is he who is destitute of knowledge, and the weak is the unpure.

The glory of God hides the Word, but the glory of a king honors commands. He who possesses the glory of God, he called the glory of God, and he who possesses the glory of the heavenly king, he called the glory of a king. For they hide the Word of God within themselves, so that they might not sin and [so that they] might honor the commands through which they act. Often we have noted this: that those possessing virtues or vices are named by the virtues or the vices. Thus, 'The Lord is just and loves justice' [Psalm 11:7] refers to the just, instead of the just ones; and 'The fear of the Lord hates injustice, pride, and arrogance' [Proverbs 8:13], that is, the unjust, the insolent, and the arrogant. And here too, he called the one possessing the glory of God 'the glory of God' and the one possessing the glory of the king 'the glory of a king.' Or perhaps he says 'glory of God' regarding the one glorifying God, and 'glory of a king' regarding the one glorifying the king, so that the saying might be such: the one glorifying God...
one establishes his own mind in righteousness

title: The Varied Names of the Soul's States
english: impassive
To stand in judgment is not good. Just as cold water is unpleasing to a soul that thirsts, so is a good message from far off the earth, and so is the knowledge of God from the earth pleasant.

Just as if someone were to break open a spring and enjoy the outlet of water, so a just man falls disorderly before the thought of the thoughts of the ungodly; his falls are called such and such, his risings, his seat, his standing; and others his walking and some of his obstacles are named; and others hard and soft and fragrant and sweet and bitter and smooth and straight and crooked; and again some of his are called thorns and briars, others light and darkness and life and death, others diseases and healths; and others again are named falsehood and truth; and many other names the Scripture sets down according to the soul and the thoughts of it.

But what it sets down against it, as it is possible to say a few of many, these are they: mind, soul, heart, man, man, woman, slave, servant, father, son, spirit, eye, mouth, lip, tongue, larynx, belly, bosom, arm, finger, wood, nose, sheep, ram, shepherd; and there are more names of the soul, which it is not possible now to set down because the nature of the scholia does not permit prolixity. There, therefore, a just mind falls before the devil, receiving an unclean thought or a false dogma. And David says: 'Before him shall all those descending into the earth fall' (Ps 102:7); but this fall contains true knowledge and pure thoughts.
Just as a city with its walls cast down and without walls, so a man who does nothing by intention. 'Will' is spoken here for the inclination of the heart toward the better.
Just as a whip to a horse and a goad to a donkey, so a rod chastises the lawless. The rod is now a symbol of punishment.

He who sends a word through a foolish angel makes a dream of his own ways. It is not necessary to give the holy things to dogs, nor to cast pearls before swine (Mt 7:6). Having removed the journey of the legs and the lawlessness from the mouth of the foolish, remove the bad way and make a long distance of false knowledge from it. He who releases a stone from a sling is like one giving glory to a foolish person. Knowledge will not fit a fool and...

title: Virtue, Knowledge, and the Perils of the Soul
english: A stone is worthless in a golden setting.

Much is covered by the flesh of fools, for their ecstasy is crushed. If the ecstasy of fools, by which they were beside themselves for God (cf. Luke 16:15), is crushed, having become pure again, they approach God; for 'all flesh shall see the salvation of God.' One must note here that he named the thickened souls from the evil flesh of fools. So also the Lord says: 'My spirit shall not remain in these men because they are flesh' (cf. Romans 8:3).

Like a dog when it rushes upon its own vomit and becomes loathsome, so a fool, having turned back to his own sin by his own wickedness, is like a dog eating its own vomit after casting away his wickedness and turning again toward it.

Having hidden a sluggish hand in his lap, he will not be able to bring it to the mouth. If 'a tree of life grows from the fruits of righteousness' (cf. Rev 22:2), everyone hiding righteousness with unrighteousness will not eat from this tree.
Like one holding a dog's leash, so is the one presiding over another's judgment. Use this saying for those being voted for some unworthy ones in Jerusalem or by lot (cf. Prov 27:17).
Fire flourishes in many woods; but where there is no hot-tempered one, the fight rests. He said the hot-tempered, hot-tempered one.
Smooth lips cover a sad heart. A pure heart will not seize sadness; for he has driven away corrupt desires from it.

If the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded by him. Our Satan sometimes entreats us, tickling us through unclean thoughts and throwing himself upon us with the smoothness of pleasure, and sometimes indeed raising a voice truly loud as if having been defeated, one whom one must not obey having the war against us.
For there are seven evils in his heart. These evils oppose the seven spirits.
A soul being in abundance plays with masters; but a soul in need, the bitter things seem sweet to it. A pure soul enjoys knowledge; but an unclean soul thinks false knowledge to be true knowledge.
Like a bird when it falls from its own nest, so a man is enslaved when he is made a stranger from his own places.

Virtue and knowledge are of the heart, from which being estranged a man falls into wickedness and ignorance and becomes a slave, since 'everyone practicing sin is a slave of sin' (John 8:34). The heart is delighted by perfumes, wines, and incenses; but the soul is shattered by accidents. The impassive Mind delights in diverse wisdom; but the empassioned mind will fall into ignorance.

Do not abandon your friend and your fellow-countryman; 'They have left me the spring of living water and have dug for themselves cisterns' (Jeremiah 2:13). Do not enter the house of your brother in misfortune; such was the one who entered the wedding feasts and did not have wedding clothes (Matthew 22:11). A near friend is better than a brother far from home. Better is the one joined to me through true knowledge than the one joined to me only through nature.

Take away his garment, for an insolent man passes by who plunders what belongs to others. This is that which is said in the Gospel: 'And from him who has not, even what he seems to have will be taken away' (Luke 16:34). This shows, in my opinion, the intellectual remnants of virtues and the knowledge of God being taken from men who have used them badly.

He who plants a fig tree will eat its fruits; but he who guards his Lord will be honored. Our Lord is the fig tree; for its fruit heals leprosy. If you dishonor the fool in the midst of a sitting, you will not escape his foolishness. Not dishonoring the fool will not turn him from his foolishness, but rather you are teaching him what kind of dishonor foolishness brings to a stranger.

Knowingly recognize the souls of your flock and understand your heart with your wise flocks; for they do not hand over strength and power to a man for an age, nor from generation to generation. Attend to yourself and direct your virtues, for men do not always prevail in them, nor do they transition healthily from virtue to virtue or from knowledge to knowledge, as the human condition does not easily receive this. Since he speaks of generations regarding virtues and knowledges, according to which the saints are born, he shows through what he writes: 'A generation of wisdom, the fear of the Lord, and wealth and glory and life' (Psalm 112:3).
